Suresh Prasad Gupta & Ors.
 Vs.
 Union of India & Ors.

 Mr.Ashoke Banerjee, Sr. Advocate
Mr.Rahul Karmakar
Ms.Gargi Goswami,

...for Petitioner
 Mr. Ashok Kumar Chakraborty, Sr.Advocate
 Mr. Sanajit Kumar Ghosh,
 ...for Respondent
Mr. Amitesh Banerjee, Sr. Standing Counsel Mr. Sanjiv Kumar Trivedi Mr. Rudrajit Sarkar, ...for
Respondent No. 7 (Irctc)
This writ petition is taken up for final hearing.
The parties are allowed to file affidavits.
A writing dated January 25, 2018 of the Railways is under challenge.
Learned senior advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that, the petitioners are valid commission agents.
Such agency has not been terminated.
The petitioners hold valid licence to undertake their activities.

Such licence not being terminated and no notice of eviction being issued,
the petitioners cannot be evicted.
He draws the attention of the Court to the various documents relied upon in the supplementary affidavit as also in the affidavit filed by the Railways in support of his contentions.
The Railways and the IRCTC are represented.

sentences.text: Learned senior advocate appearing for the Railways submits that, the petitioners, at best, can claim themselves to be commission agents.
However, such agency stands terminated with the attainment of the prescribed age of 60 years.
In any event, none of these petitioners have any valid commercial licence to claim that, they are commission agents.
He draws the attention of the Court to the various documents annexed to the pleadings of the parties.
Learned senior advocate for the IRCTC submits that, his client has not been served with the copy of the writ petition.
The writ petition was taken up for consideration on February 2, 2018 when an interim order was passed.
The affidavit of service filed shows that, the petitioners have not even attempted to serve IRCTC who is a respondent.
It is obligatory on the part of the petitioners, more so when they have obtained an interim order, to serve the non-appearing respondents.
The petitioners have failed to do so.
On this ground alone, the interim order deserves to be vacated and is vacated.
However, that is not the sole ground to vacate the interim order.
So far as the merits of the matter are concerned, it is found that, the claims of the petitioners being commission agents are misplaced.
They have licences undr the Food Standard and Safety Act.
They do not possess any commercial licence.
Railways had formulated a policy of absorption of vendors as regular employees.
Opportunities for such absorption were afforded to each of the petitioners.
They choose either not to participate or did not satisfy the criteria.
They were not absorbed.
The Court need not go into the reasons as to why the petitioners were not absorbed.
Be that as it may, the petitioners not having any right to occupy any part or portion of the Railway property, they are not entitled to remain thereat.
So far as the non-service of notice of eviction is concerned, it appears that, the Railways are exercising powers under Section 147 of the Indian Railways Act, 1989.
No interference is called for on such aspect also.
In such circumstances, W.P. 2595 (W) OF 2018 is dismissed without any order as to costs.
Interim orders stand vacated.
Urgent certified website copies of this order, if applied for, be made available to the parties upon compliance of the requisite formalities.
( DEBANGSU BASAK, J. )
